newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian pound continues rising vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian pound continues rising vs dollar.

text.p: The Egyptian pound firmed again against the dollar in a short private-sector market with more offers of the U.S. currency on Tuesday, bankers said.

Bankers said the pound shortage was a result of treasury bill auctions. The central bank has been auctioning for the past three weeks t-bills that are worth about 300 million pounds more than the total of the maturing bills.
The latest offer is for 91-day bills worth 1.1 billion pounds at Wednesday's auction, replacing bills worth 665.3 million maturing on Thursday.
Private-sector bankers said the dollar ranged from 3.3945 to 3.3960 pounds bid and from 3.3960 to 3.3980 pounds offered in the interbank market.
A survey of five actively trading banks gave average rates of 3.3951 pounds bid and 3.3971 pounds offered. These averages compare to 3.3962 pounds bid and 3.3975 offered on Monday.
The central bank calculated the average exchange rate at midday as 3.392727 buy and 3.398496 sell.
